sequence_description: Direct-endpoint attack: attempt to inject authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none). The auth endpoint should reject the unsigned request object to preserve proof integrity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none), enabling parameter injection without integrity protection.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none), enabling parameter injection without integrity protection.

sequence_description: I2: Control vs attack for token freshness. First obtain a valid access token via password grant, then attempt to use the same user credentials after disabling the user (config change) to ensure new tokens cannot be minted. This tests whether Keycloak incorrectly allows token issuance for a disabled principal (freshness/validity of credential artifacts after administrative invalidation).
description: [LLM-Judge] Test could not evaluate token freshness/disabled-user behavior because the OIDC client was never created (client creation failed), causing all password-grant attempts to fail with invalid_client.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Test could not evaluate token freshness/disabled-user behavior because the OIDC client was never created (client creation failed), causing all password-grant attempts to fail with invalid_client.

sequence_description: I4 attack: Empty-sub / missing-sub confusion via OIDC request object. Attempt to get two distinct authorization requests to map to the same downstream subject due to empty or missing subject-like identifiers being treated as a default/anonymous principal.
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC request object with an empty/missing `sub`-like identifier was accepted (HTTP 200), which may enable subject-confusion if downstream mapping treats empty subject as a default/anonymous principal.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC request object with an empty/missing `sub`-like identifier was accepted (HTTP 200), which may enable subject-confusion if downstream mapping treats empty subject as a default/anonymous principal.

sequence_description: I5: Attempt scope/parameter injection via unsigned request object (alg=none). If accepted, attacker can request broader scopes than intended without integrity protection.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) was accepted and allowed scope/parameter injection, enabling privilege escalation via untrusted request parameters.
